name: Tawang Monastery
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Perched at about 10,000 feet overlooking the Tawang Chu valley, it houses a large golden Buddha statue, ancient scriptures, and is a major spiritual and cultural center for the Monpa people.
facts: Second largest monastery in the world after Potala Palace
Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama nearby
Requires Inner Line Permit for visitors

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude lake at about 3,708 m on the road from Tawang to Bum La Pass. Formed by an earthquake that submerged trees, popularly called Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood film was shot here. Known for submerged tree trunks and scenic views near the Indo-China border.
facts: Special Army permit required beyond certain points
Accessible mainly in clear weather with SUVs

name: Sela Pass
description: High mountain pass at 4,170 m (13,700 ft) on the border between Tawang and West Kameng districts. Gateway to Tawang, often snow-covered, with Sela Lake nearby. One of the highest motorable passes on the route from Guwahati/Bomdila to Tawang.
facts: Named after a local legend involving Sela and Nura

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: About 100-metre high curtain waterfall near Jang town, roughly 40 km southeast of Tawang. Fed by the Nuranang Chu originating near Sela Pass. Also called Bong Bong Falls; popular stop on the way to Tawang with a small hydel plant nearby.
facts: Also known as Jung Falls or Bong Bong Falls
Song from Bollywood film Koyla shot nearby
Easily accessible from the main highway

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Nyingma/Gelug monastery near Tawang town, established around 1489. Birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama, Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Smaller and quieter than the main Tawang Monastery, offering a peaceful spiritual experience.
facts: Less crowded alternative to the main monastery

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Memorial in the form of a Buddhist chorten dedicated to Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Located near Tawang town with names of martyrs inscribed; features light and sound shows and panoramic valley views.

name: Gorsam Chorten
description: Large ancient Buddhist stupa near Zemithang village in Tawang district. Modeled after Boudhanath Stupa in Nepal; believed built between 12th-14th century by Lama Sangye Pradhar. Site of the annual Gorsam Kora festival.
facts: Gorsam Kora festival attracts many devotees

name: Zemithang
description: Remote border village in Tawang district near the trijunction of India, Tibet, and Bhutan. Known for Monpa culture, Gorsam Chorten, and as the place where the Dalai Lama first entered India in 1959. Offers pristine valleys and traditional village life.
facts: Historically significant for Dalai Lama's entry
Requires permits due to border proximity

name: Pangateng Tso (PT Tso Lake)
description: Serene high-altitude glacial lake at around 3,650-4,000 m on the road toward Bum La Pass. Less crowded than Madhuri Lake, with clear reflective waters, alpine meadows, and mountain views. Maintained with pathways by the Army.
facts: Also known as Pankang Teng Tso

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base in Tawang district. Nestled in the Eastern Himalayas at about 3,000 m, serving as the gateway to monasteries, lakes, and border areas. Features local markets, Monpa culture, and views of the surrounding mountains.
facts: Connected via NH-13 over Sela Pass
Base for day trips to nearby attractions
